decision_note: Senna mexicana dissertation measures extrafloral-nectar-mediated ant defence, herbivory, pollinator activity and reproductive fitness; retain for defence-pollination functional-boundary adjudication.
Penstemon digitalis dissertation explicitly studies floral scent as a signal mediating interactions with pollinators and antagonists; retain for shared floral-signal adjudication.
Linaria vulgaris dissertation directly studies pollination and nectar robbing in the same floral system; retain for pollinator-robber ecology and fitness adjudication.
Aphid/parasitoid/caterpillar interaction thesis concerns trophic interactions on plants without a focal floral trait/reward or pollinator service channel.
Faba-bean crop-rotation thesis focuses pollinators and pollination services without a focal plant antagonist/exploiter response.
Focused review on global-change effects on floral traits integrates pollinator and non-pollinator selective pressures; retain as relevant synthesis/source-chasing material.
Revisited meta-analysis directly synthesizes effects of herbivory on pollinators; retain as relevant synthesis of a core indirect mutualist-antagonist pathway.
Primary Babiana study experimentally links mammalian herbivory to inflorescence architecture and seed set in a bird-pollinated lineage; retain for herbivory-pollination trait-evolution adjudication.
Cleistogamous-herb study compares pollen source/flower type, progeny performance and seed predation but does not measure a focal pollinator service/response.
Dissertation explicitly examines effects of pollinators, herbivores and predators on floral trait evolution; retain for chapter-level multi-agent selection adjudication.
Artificial selection on whole-plant height in Brassica rapa concerns pleiotropic effects of plant height rather than a focal floral trait/reward coordinate.
Primary Vicia faba study measures effects of foliar damage on floral characteristics and pollinator visits; retain for herbivory-induced floral/pollinator pathway adjudication.
Fig-wasp study tests nematode infection of pollinating and non-pollinating fig wasps and net consequences for the fig pollination mutualism; retain for multi-party mutualist-antagonist adjudication.
Bee diet-width/sensory-morphology thesis focuses pollinator evolution rather than a focal plant antagonist/exploiter response.

Primary Epipactis study documents floral aphid mimicry, aphid infestation and aphidophagous hoverfly pollination across populations; retain for tritrophic indirect-defence-to-pollination adjudication.

Focused Ecology Letters synthesis on floral scent and insect chemical communication spans pollinator attraction and antagonistic insect interactions; retain as relevant synthesis/source-chasing material.
Dissertation explicitly studies evolution of flower size/flowering behaviour under pollination and pre-dispersal seed predation; retain for same-trait mutualist-antagonist adjudication.
Araceae phylogenetic study concerns evolution of pollinator-plant interaction types without a focal plant antagonist/exploiter channel.
Review of mutual services focuses mutualistic interactions rather than a focal plant pollinator-antagonist floral coordinate.

Ficus microcarpa dissertation includes pollinating and numerous non-pollinating fig wasps, enemy release and seed/pollinator predation across ranges; retain for fig mutualism-antagonist community adjudication.
Bdallophytum floral-biology study concerns connective appendages and pollination without a focal plant antagonist/exploiter response.
Study concerns a parasitic beetle mimicking floral scent to attract bees; the focal organism/trait is the beetle mimic, not a plant floral coordinate.
Preprint identity of the parasitic-beetle floral-illusion study; focal trait belongs to the beetle rather than a plant floral coordinate.

Primary high-Andean flowerpiercer study quantifies how floral traits predict nectar robbing and pollen transport, allowing the same visitor guild to span antagonistic and pollinating roles; retain for role-boundary adjudication.
Primary Parnassia study explicitly tests nectar-mimic staminodes that attract both pollinators and florivorous beetles; retain as a strong shared-trait functional-dilemma candidate.
